'''Tezuka Mitsumori''' (手塚 光盛, ? - {{ill|Juei|en|Juei|qid=Q598057|lt=Juei}} 3rd year (1184)) was a {{ill|bushi|ja|武士|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/samurai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1975935}} during the late {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}. He was a member of the {{ill|Kanasashi clan|ja|金刺氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanasashi clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 金刺部氏}}, who served as ritualists of the {{ill|Shimosha|ja|下社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of the {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}}. He was also known as Tezuka Betto's son (or nephew) and had an elder brother, {{ill|Kana Moritomo|ja|金刺盛澄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanemasa Morizumi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11646497}}. His common name was Tarō.

In the {{ill|The Tale of the Heike|en|The Tale of the Heike|qid=Q830740|lt=The Tale of the Heike}}, Mitsumori is identified as a resident of {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}}, specifically in the {{ill|Suwa District, Nagano|en|Suwa District, Nagano|qid=Q1131473|lt=Suwa District}}. Recent studies suggest that the Tezuka clan, including Mitsumori, was based in the {{ill|Q86729932|ja|手塚 (上田市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tezuka area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q86729932}} of {{ill|Ueda, Nagano|en|Ueda, Nagano|qid=Q844852|lt=Ueda, Nagano}} due to the presence of relics such as a residence site, {{ill|Yabusame|en|Yabusame|qid=Q1886157|lt=yabusame}} structures, a five-story stupa, and temples connected to Mitsumori’s legacy.<ref>Ueda City Historical Records (2001), "Manors and Samurai of Ueda," p. 27-31.</ref> However, no descendants of the Tezuka clan currently reside in the area. Tezuka-chō in {{ill|Kaga, Ishikawa|ja|石川県加賀市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaga, Ishikawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} is named after Tezuka Tarō Mitsumori.

== Career ==
In {{ill|Jishō|en|Jishō|qid=Q1194671|lt=Jishō}} 4th year (1180), when Minamoto no Yoshinaka raised an army, Mitsumori joined as a prominent commander. In {{ill|Juei|en|Juei|qid=Q598057|lt=Juei}} 2nd year (1183), he participated in the {{ill|Battle of Shinohara|en|Battle of Shinohara|qid=Q2889980|lt=Battle of Shinohara}}. An episode from this battle is notable in the {{ill|The Tale of the Heike|en|The Tale of the Heike|qid=Q830740|lt=The Tale of the Heike}}, where Mitsumori defeated {{ill|Sanemori Saitō|ja|斎藤実盛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitō Sanemori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3472140}}.

Sanemori, concealing his old age by dyeing his white hair black, fought valiantly in the colors of the general {{ill|Taira no Koremori|en|Taira no Koremori|qid=Q3055506|lt=Taira no Koremori}}. After a fierce duel, Mitsumori brought Sanemori's head back to Yoshinaka's camp. When the head was washed, the dye faded, revealing white hair. Recognizing the man as his savior during childhood, Yoshinaka wept openly.<ref>The Tale of the Heike.</ref>

In {{ill|Juei|en|Juei|qid=Q598057|lt=Juei}} 3rd year (1184), during the {{ill|Battle of Awazu|en|Battle of Awazu|qid=Q2237381|lt=Battle of Awazu}}, Mitsumori fought against the armies of {{ill|Minamoto no Noriyori|en|Minamoto no Noriyori|qid=Q3142238|lt=Minamoto no Noriyori}} and {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|en|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|qid=Q310445|lt=Minamoto no Yoshitsune}}, dying alongside his lord Yoshinaka. He was one of the last loyal retainers to Yoshinaka.

== Descendants and Legacy ==
Tezuka Mitsumori is associated with several legends and remains:
* His grave is located in {{ill|Q86729932|ja|手塚 (上田市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tezuka area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q86729932}}, {{ill|Ueda, Nagano|en|Ueda, Nagano|qid=Q844852|lt=Ueda, Nagano}}.
* The Tezuka clan changed their surname to Tetsuka and established a memorial for Mitsumori in Osaka's {{ill|Tezukayama|ja|帝塚山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tezukayama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11481044}}.

Mitsumori's lineage is said to include:
* Tezuka Mitsuharu, a descendant who served as a {{ill|Rangaku|en|Rangaku|qid=Q877637|lt=rangaku}} scholar.
* {{ill|Osamu Tezuka|en|Osamu Tezuka|qid=Q193300|lt=Osamu Tezuka}}, a famous manga artist, is believed to be a 9th-generation descendant.<ref>Osamu Tezuka’s work "Phoenix" ("Civil War Chapter") references his lineage.</ref>
